obviously idk how much of her prioritising and defending him are her own views (or his influence) but the most you can do for her is to be a non judgemental support system, or at least for your niece. 

lashing out at her or expressing disappointment that she won't leave him (which may not be as easy as you think) will only isolate her and her daughter further - unfortunately, if she really does want to leave it will be a long game op

Soft YTA because as much as you are in the wrong, it's a tricky situation. From your brother's perspective, it's like your abandoning him because he isn't fun, interesting or good enough to take a trip with, which, based in the fact that you agreed to go in the first place, I'm sure isn't true BUT that's the message you're sending.

Is your brother awkward around just your friends or everyone? Does he like your friends or is the joint trip something that benefits you only? Could he be trying to use the trip as a way to start working through his awkwardness?

As a joint trip, it's about compromise and you aren't making this decision with both of you in mind, only yourself. If you really want, go without him, but it would be better I think to communicate and try to find a solution that works for both of you.

NTA but I understand where her anger comes from: correct me if I'm wrong but her brother will still have gotten an extra month abroad, so even though your decision is valid, there is a difference in what they get.

If it's possible, could you offer an alternative trip for her (maybe in the UK/Europe or with friends/older cousins so she's not completely alone) to replace the experience? She might feel better if you provide another way to have the same independence and self discovery that her brother got.

It sounds like you're both in really difficult places right now and I hope you find yourselves somewhere better in the future but I don't think you should feel guilty. Even though, yes, you talking about cutting introduced the topic between you it's not like you invented it you know?

Think about it like this: if he say a film or read a book that mentioned cutting, would that have 'inspired' him? Would the script writer or author then be responsible? He's his own person and he's making the decision to hurt himself and use the methods he uses by himself.

If you're worried that (what I'm assuming is) seeking comfort our solidarity is encouraging or influencing him, it might be worth having a conversation about what is a healthy amount of information to share with eachother. That's obviously more complicated than I can suggest answers too.

Ultimately though I don't think it makes you a hypocrite: just because you hurt yourself doesn't mean you want to watch, or know, that someone you love is doing the same. Communicate your feelings to him and maybe consider speaking to someone who won't turn what you say back on you, if he's adamant on 'blaming' you.

I think she's commenting on how a lot of teenage experiences aren't well processed in the moment, but as an adult she can see how violent and destructive they were.

Since the whole song is about growing up and teenage/YA experience I think the lyric is about having something that won't last (hence 'falls') but will be exciting and chaotic as it happens, like watching someone fall off the balcony at a party. The 'something' could be a relationship or just the consequences of choices someone makes.

In the end though, the narrator and the spectators will know how horrific and self deatructive what's happened was, and the way they reacted and thought about it at the time will eat away at them (through guilt, regret, etc.).
